name: IDT - In-Context Decision Transformer: Reinforcement Learning via Hierarchical Chain-of-Thought
venue: ICML 2024 (Proceedings of the 41st International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 235:19871-19885)
authors_affiliation: Sili Huang, Jifeng Hu, Hechang Chen, Bo Yang (Jilin University, China); Lichao Sun (Lehigh University, USA). Lead author Sili Huang. Affiliations inferred from author records and the China National Key R&D Program / NSFC / Jilin Province funding in the acknowledgments [uncertain on exact per-author affiliation mapping].
maintained_repo_url: N/A (single-paper code repo; not a continuously-updated leaderboard/list)
task_domain: decision-making / offline-to-online reinforcement learning (in-context RL). Continuous control (MuJoCo locomotion) and discrete navigation (Grid World) tasks.
problem_setting: Offline-trained, test-time-online in-context RL. The agent is trained by supervised sequence prediction on a fixed offline dataset of (possibly sub-optimal) trajectories, then at test time self-improves on unseen tasks purely in-context (no gradient updates) by rolling out multiple episodes and conditioning on an across-episodic context. Single-agent; supervision is the offline trajectories' low-level actions (autoregressive). Online phase involves no parameter updates, only forward passes.
what_is_retrieved: Across-episodic experiences: multiple historical trajectories (a 'chain of experience') arranged in ascending order of returns, reconstructed by IDT into a high-level 'hierarchical chain of experience' of high-level decisions (latent vectors z) rather than low-level actions.
retrieval_grounding: GROWING/episodic memory the agent itself produces. The across-episodic context is the agent's own rolled-out trajectories accumulated during test-time trial-and-error (plus optionally external demonstration prompts in the case study). It is not a static external corpus/KB.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Neither a top-k ranking nor a completeness-recovery objective. The context is a fixed-size window of the most recent n=4 episodes; 'selection' is implicit via the Transformer's causal self-attention over this window. The objective is to predict a higher-return next trajectory conditioned on the ordered context (chain-of-hindsight-style return improvement).
cbr_cycle_coverage: N/A (not framed as CBR). Loosely: Retrieve (attend over past episodes) and Reuse (condition generation on them) are present; Revise/Retain are not classic CBR operations (memory is an append-only rolling episode buffer, not a curated case base).
explicit_cbr_grounding: False. The work does not frame itself as case-based reasoning and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza / Kolodner; it is framed as in-context RL / hierarchical RL / chain-of-experience / chain-of-hindsight.
retrieval_unit: Reconstructed (state/observation, high-level-decision z, reward, completion) tuples at the high-level (one per c environment steps), forming high-level sub-trajectories across episodes. Baselines (AT/AD) use per-step (return, observation, action, reward, completion) tuples; IDT's unit is the high-level decision token summarizing a c-step segment.
index_source: Online/test-time-induced growing memory: the across-episodic context is built from trajectories the agent itself generates during the test-time trial-and-error rollout (and at training, sampled minibatches of offline trajectories). No offline-induced static retrieval index.
index_structure_topology: Flat ordered sequence (context-keyed): n=4 trajectories concatenated and sorted in ascending order of total return, consumed as a single token sequence by causal self-attention. No vector index, graph, or hierarchical store; the only 'hierarchy' is temporal (high-level decision over c low-level steps).
retriever_type: Implicit: Transformer causal self-attention over the in-context sequence acts as the 'search/memory' mechanism (no explicit BM25/dense retriever). The paper frames self-attention as the search over memory of past experiences.
retriever_learning_signal: None as an explicit retriever; selection is fixed (most-recent-n episodes, return-sorted). The whole model (including the attention that does the implicit search) is trained end-to-end by supervised action-prediction loss (cross-entropy for discrete, MSE for continuous actions); there is no contrastive/RL retriever-training signal for selection itself.
query_construction: Implicit: the current observation o_t plus the past across-episodic trajectories serve as the conditioning context; the Making Decisions module predicts the next high-level decision z_t given o_t and past trajectories. No explicit query string is formed; the 'query' is the autoregressive position conditioned on the ordered experience context plus the target return token.
query_granularity: Two-level / both. High level: a high-level decision z is queried/generated every c steps (trajectory/segment level) by the Making Decisions module; low level: actions are generated per step within each c-step segment by the Decisions to Go module conditioned on z.
when_to_retrieve: Iterative / fixed schedule. The across-episodic context is refreshed continuously as new episodes are rolled out; a new high-level decision is produced on a fixed schedule (every c steps). Not uncertainty-triggered or learned-router.
retrieval_trigger_signal: Fixed schedule: a high-level decision is generated once every c steps (c=10 for D4RL and Large Grid World, c=5 for standard Grid World), and the context window holds the most recent n=4 episodes. No confidence/attention/classifier trigger.
reranking: None. No explicit reranking stage; trajectories are ordered by total return (ascending) before being placed in context, but this is a fixed sort, not a learned reranker.
retrieved_context_refinement: Reconstruction/compression rather than rerank/distill: IDT compresses the per-step action sequence into a high-level chain of high-level decisions (one z per c steps), drastically shortening the context (smaller than one episode length). No relevance filtering or distractor removal.
index_content_separation: N/A (no separate lightweight index vs heavy content; the context IS the content).
how_retrieved_used: Prompt/context augmentation as conditioning for autoregressive generation: the across-episodic high-level chain of experience conditions the Making Decisions module to predict the next high-level decision z; z is then a latent conditional input to the Decisions to Go module that autoregressively generates the next c low-level actions. Effectively latent-token (high-level decision) injection plus in-context experience conditioning.
planning_integration: Hierarchical, plan-then-act with interleaving: a high-level decision (sub-goal) is generated first (Making Decisions), then it guides multi-step low-level action generation (Decisions to Go), and executed actions are encoded back into high-level decisions (Reviewing Decisions) to update the across-episodic context for the next cycle. Retrieval (the across-episodic context) is woven in at the high-level subtask boundary every c steps.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: Per-high-level-decision (every c steps): the implicit search over experience occurs at each high-level decision boundary (one high-level decision per c-step segment), not per low-level action; this is the source of the efficiency gain.
adaptation_mechanism: N/A as classic CBR adaptation. Closest analogue: latent / execution-conditioned generation. Retrieved experience is reused by conditioning autoregressive generation; the Reviewing Decisions module re-encodes executed (or externally provided demonstration) actions into high-level decisions to adapt them into the agent's high-level abstraction.
retrieved_item_representation: Latent / soft tokens at the high level: high-level decisions are continuous vectors z sampled from a multivariate Gaussian (with reparameterization), injected as conditioning tokens; the underlying raw experience is (return, observation, decision, reward, completion) token embeddings.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Distilled/abstract: high-level decisions (latent sub-goals) abstracting c-step low-level action segments, rather than raw per-step trajectories (as in baselines AT/AD).
noise_robustness_mechanism: Implicit robustness via return-ordered chain-of-hindsight conditioning and learning from sub-optimal data: prior (lower-return) trajectories act as negative-rated examples to predict higher-return ones; end-to-end supervised training over sub-optimal offline data. No dedicated relevance evaluator / distractor-aware module.
memory_type: episodic (across-episodic rolling context of recent trajectories) with a latent hierarchical abstraction (high-level decisions). In-context memory, not an external persistent store.
write_back: True (in-context only): executed actions are reviewed/encoded into high-level decisions and appended to the across-episodic context for the next trial-and-error cycle. This is in-context state growth, not persistent gradient/parameter or external-DB write-back.
online_growth: Yes within the rolling context window: the context grows as new episodes are rolled out during test time (capped at the most recent n=4 episodes). The model parameters are frozen at test time (no gradient updates); only the in-context experience grows/rotates.
write_back_trigger: Per-segment/per-episode (fixed schedule): after each c-step segment the executed actions are encoded into a high-level decision (Reviewing Decisions), and completed episodes are added to the across-episodic context. Not gated by success/failure or self-critique.
failure_experience_usage: Success+failure mixed via return ordering: lower-return (effectively 'failed' or sub-optimal) trajectories are kept in the context as negative-rated examples (ascending-return chain of experience) to drive the model toward higher-return predictions. No explicit failure-only corrective rules.
memory_evolution_update: Append-and-rotate within a fixed-size window (most recent n=4 episodes, return-sorted); high-level decisions are re-encoded each cycle. No dedup-merge, delta-update, or learned forgetting/pruning of stored entries.
retrieval_as_learned_policy: No. Selection of context (most-recent-n, return-sorted) is fixed; it is not an RL/learned retrieval policy. The high-level decision policy is learned end-to-end by supervised sequence prediction (not a soft Q-learning / M-MDP retrieval policy).
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: No. Single-agent private in-context memory; no cross-agent or cross-framework experience sharing.
benchmarks: Grid World (Darkroom, Darkroom Hard, Darkroom Dynamic, Dark Key-to-Door, and their Large 40x40 variants with 10x episode length); D4RL MuJoCo locomotion (HalfCheetah, Hopper, Walker) with Medium, Medium-Replay, and Medium-Expert datasets.
benchmark_family: decision-RL (D4RL MuJoCo) and embodied/navigation-style grid (Grid World / Darkroom family). Long-horizon decision-making benchmarks (episode lengths 20-1000 steps).
baselines: In-context RL: Agentic Transformer (AT, Hao Liu 2023), Algorithm Distillation (AD, Laskin et al. 2023). TD learning: TD3+BC, TD3. Imitation learning: Behavior Cloning (BC-10%), Decision Transformer (DT). Baseline numbers for D4RL taken from the AT paper and the D4RL paper.
key_metrics: D4RL normalized score (100 = expert); Grid World episodic return / self-improvement curve over 50 episodes; training time per 10k gradient updates; test/evaluation time (minutes) for 10 D4RL episodes / 50 Grid World episodes; speedup factor (x) over baselines.
headline_result: Online evaluation time 36x faster than baselines on D4RL and 27x faster on (Large) Grid World, while achieving state-of-the-art / competitive task performance. D4RL Total Average normalized score 87.90 +/- 1.06 for IDT (Ours) vs AT 85.21, BC-10% 80.65, TD3+BC 84.83, AD 82.84, DT 77.49, TD3 70.28.
ablations: Computing-cost breakdown (Table 3): on HalfCheetah (context 4000), AT testing 234.20 min (37x) and AD 173.11 min (28x) vs IDT 6.29 min; on Large Dark Key-to-Door (context 2000), AT 167.07 min (27x) vs IDT 6.18 min. Parameter sensitivity on high-level decision frequency c (c=1,5,10,15,20): stable in dense-reward D4RL, larger c better in sparse-reward Grid World. Context-size analysis: across-episodic context of ~4 episodes needed for self-improvement to emerge. Case study (Fig. 5): Reviewing Decisions module lets IDT exploit external demonstration prompts (epsilon-greedy data from random to optimal) to accelerate in-context self-improvement.
evaluation_decoupling: No. There are no intrinsic retrieval metrics (Recall@k/nDCG) since retrieval is implicit self-attention over in-context experience; only end-to-end task return/score and compute/time metrics are reported.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Primarily outcome (final normalized score / episodic return) plus efficiency/process-cost metrics (training and testing time, speedup, context length). Self-improvement curves over episodes capture process-level improvement trajectory; no reasoning-faithfulness or step-wise retrieval-accuracy metrics.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Central contribution: IDT cuts test-time evaluation cost ~36x (D4RL) and ~27x (Large Grid World) by shortening across-episodic context to high-level decisions (context smaller than one episode). E.g., HalfCheetah test time 6.29 min (IDT) vs 234.20 min (AT); training ~21.9 h (IDT) vs ~36.2 h (AT). Lower memory requirement than AT (AT could not be trained in D4RL on the authors' hardware). Self-attention complexity is quadratic in sequence length, so context shortening yields the speedup.
context_budget_and_selection_count: Fixed window: n=4 across-episodic trajectories (10 trajectories for some short Grid World tasks). Task horizons T range 20-1000 steps; maximum context reaches ~20000 tokens for baselines, but IDT keeps context smaller than one episode by using one high-level decision per c steps (c=10 for D4RL/Large Grid World, c=5 for standard Grid World). Selection is fixed-k (most-recent-n, return-sorted), not adaptive.
benchmark_construction_and_size: N/A (uses existing benchmarks). Grid World data: 60 randomly-created tasks per environment, ~1M timesteps each, collected from DQN learning histories; D4RL Medium/Medium-Replay/Medium-Expert ~1-2M timesteps from medium/expert/replay policies.
builds_on: Decision Transformer (Chen et al. 2021); Agentic Transformer / chain of experience (Hao Liu 2023); Algorithm Distillation (Laskin et al. 2023); Decision-Pretrained Transformer (Lee et al. 2023b); Chain of Hindsight (Liu et al. 2023); hierarchical RL with continuous sub-goals (Nachum et al. 2018, HIRO); Multi-Game Decision Transformer / Grid World (Lee et al. 2022).
contrasts_with: Agentic Transformer (AT) and Algorithm Distillation (AD): IDT contrasts by operating trial-and-error on high-level decisions instead of the smallest per-step actions, avoiding excessively long across-episodic sequences. Also contrasts with single-episode-context Decision Transformer (no self-improvement) and offline TD methods (TD3+BC) that require gradient updates / are not in-context.
lineage: Group F (decision_memory_rl): in-context / across-episodic RL with self-improvement via in-context (episodic) memory. Sits in the Algorithm-Distillation / Agentic-Transformer lineage of treating RL as across-episodic sequence prediction, extending it with a hierarchical (high-level-decision) chain of experience for efficiency on long-horizon tasks.
